tossups.text: One character visits this location on earth by disguising himself as a toad before he whispers into the ears of a sleeping woman. That character leaves this location after the descent of a pair of golden scales. After achieving a victory at this location, a villain returns home and hears hisses instead of applause and sees a grove of trees have all their fruit turn into ash. A storyteller speaking to one of this location's inhabitants describes how Abdiel tried to mediate a conflict between a loser that fell for nine days through Chaos. That dude telling a story at this location describes how the winning army in that conflict used mountains to bury their foes. While speaking to its inhabitants, Raphael invokes Urania to describe the Creation of the world. A sexual encounter between its two inhabitants results in guilt and shame being exposed for the first time; that happened because they both ate a piece of forbidden fruit. For 10 points, identify this location that Adam and Eve lose in a poem by John Milton.

In one form, this deity was a lover of Mami who commanded seven warriors representing the Pleiades called the Sebitti. This figure's father aided him in his most famous quest by giving him seven pairs of demons, and this figure's epithet of Engidudu means "lord who prowls by night." This deity is often identified by a lion sickle and a lion mace, and his form of Erra is a god of plague and war. In one story this deity builds a throne from fine wood for his future wife, and this figure is ordered not to eat with his future wife but eventually he sleeps with her for seven days. This figure was hidden in spring water by Ea to help him hide from Namtar after he returned from Irkalla. For 10 points, identify this wife of Ereshkigal and son of Enlil, the lord of the underworld in Sumerian mythology.

This brother of Deiphobus was adopted by the shepherd Agelaus after being suckled by a she-bear for nine days. His first wife Oenone refused to heal him after he was wounded by Philoctetes' arrow, and his mother Hecuba had a nightmare before giving birth to him. He once fled from a duel with Menelaus and later shot Achilles in the heel with the guidance of Apollo. He infuriated Hera and Athena by giving a golden apple to another goddess. For 10 points, name this prince who started the Trojan War by fleeing with Helen after choosing Aphrodite as the most beautiful goddess in his namesake judgment.

Edward Craig has used this philosopher's notion of "vindicatory genealogies" that uphold rather than corrode their subject. This man praised Diderot's murky picture of selfhood over Rousseau's, and argued that Thucydides, not Herodotus, invented historical time in a book that calls accuracy and sincerity the virtues of truthfulness. This man denied an "Archimedean point" from which to convince amoralists that they are mistaken in a book that distinguishes thin ethical concepts like "goodness" from thick ones like "prudence." This author of Truth and Truthfulness asked if we would judge Gauguin's abandonment of his family harshly if he'd failed as a painter in a paper that coined a term for judgment a person receives for actions outside their control. For 10 points, who wrote Ethics and the Limits of Philosophy and "Moral Luck"?

A recent boom in oil extraction in the western part of this state has created a massive need for workers and a housing shortage in its town of Williston, where the NBA's Phil Jackson played high school basketball before playing for the University of [this state]. The plains of the Red River Valley dominate the eastern portion of the state, while White Butte, located north of Theodore Roosevelt National Park, is this state's highest point. Its largest city abuts this state's eastern border, across from Moorhead, in neighboring Minnesota. For 10 points Fargo is the largest city in what state with capital at Bismarck?

Some practitioners of this faith believe that nuclear war will destroy Babylon. A sacred text of this religion begins with four chapters called Athlyi ("ATH-lee-EYE") and is called the Holy Piby ("PIE-bee"). The practices of this religion are referred to as livity, and its dietary practices are called ital ("EYE-tall"). Practitioners of this faith are divided up into several "mansions," such as Nyahbinghi ("nya-BING-ee"), the Twelve Tribes of Israel, and the Bobo Ashanti. Those not part of this religion are called "baldheads." Holy figures in this religion include Marcus Garvey and Haile Selassie ("HIGH-luh seh-LASS-ee"). For 10 points, name this religion most commonly practiced in Jamaica.

This man gave the "Beyond Vietnam" speech and organized the Montgomery bus boycott. This activist orated the "I've Been to the Mountaintop" speech a day before he was shot by James Earl Ray, while another of his speeches tells the audience to judge others by "the content of their character". For 10 points, name this civil rights activist who delivered the "I Have A Dream" Speech.

A concept proposed by this philosopher appears in the title of Philippa Foot's article introducing the trolley problem. This philosopher argued it is permissible to cause harm as a side effect of a good result in his doctrine of "double effect." This man referred to Averroes (ah-ver-OH-us) as "The Commentator" in a long book started in 1266 that expands on the "unmoved mover" argument as part of five proofs for the existence of God. For 10 points, name this Catholic philosopher who systematized Scholastic philosophy in Summa Theologica.

In 2015, a team led by Su-Yang Xu ("shoo") et al. made the first observation of one variety of these particles in crystals with broken inversion symmetry. The Nelson-Ninomiya theorem asserts that the typical method of discretizing these particles on a chiral lattice leads to doubling the number of fields. Weyl ("vile") semimetals host unusual examples of these particles, whose fields obey a canonical anti-commutation relation. An equation of motion for these particles can be expressed in Feynman slash notation to represent the gamma matrices. Applying the exchange operator flips the sign of a wavefunction of two of these particles. Two identical ones cannot occupy the same quantum state according to the Pauli exclusion principle. For 10 points, name these particles with half-integer spin.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on electrons by saying "we want a more general answer"

tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for diaphragm and intercostal muscles. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this diaphragm-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The diaphragm is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in diaphragm and intercostal muscles.

tossups.text: In human physiology, this structure is essential for four chambers of the heart. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this atrium-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The atrium is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in four chambers of the heart.

tossups.text: A philosopher from this country described "father to son" and "ruler to subject" as two of his five fundamental human relationships, as part of his teachings in the Analects. Many philosophers from this country advocated venerating one's ancestors, a practice known as "filial piety". Taoism was developed in, for 10 points, what country where Confucius was from, and where his teachings were adopted in the Forbidden City?

This thinker collaborated with James Baldwin on the work A Rap on Race. Derek Freeman claimed people on the island of Ta'u had lied to this thinker in a work titled for her "fateful hoaxing." This thinker's most famous work analyzes the maturation of adolescent girls in the title location. For 10 points, name this American anthropologist, who wrote Coming of Age in Samoa.
acceptableAnswers: The Fateful Hoaxing of Margaret Mead

tossups.text: A place primarily dedicated to this deity is lined with five-coloured orbs called suedama ("soo-eh-dah-mah") representing jewels and holds a ceremony in which local villagers carry two white stones each to place around it. "Distant worship" from the capital accompanied the first ears of grain dedicated to this deity in a festival held in mid-October. A curved bead shaped like a comma was hung from a tree to lure this deity. That bead is stored in a shrine dedicated to this deity that is rebuilt every 20 years. This deity was shown their reflection in a bronze mirror after being tricked into leaving a cave. This deity's brother, Susanoo, gave them the grass-cutter sword Kusanagi that was passed down to Emperor Jimmu, who descended from this goddess. For 10 points, name this sun goddess, often considered the chief kami of Shintoism.
acceptableAnswers: accept Ōhirume no Muchi no Kami

tossups.text: Braunschweig et al, made a landmark synthesis of a diatomic molecule of this element using its bromide, stabilized by N-heterocyclic carbenes, from which the bromines were sequentially removed. That synthesis makes this element the third element to have a stable triple bond with itself at sufficiently high temperatures. Eberhardt, Crawford, and Lipscomb described the 3-center 2-electron bonds formed by this element in a set of molecules whose topology is described by the styx formula. A hydride of this element forms an adduct with THF, and that adduct facilitates the anti-Markovnikov addition of a water-molecule after workup with hydrogen peroxide in a reaction named for HC Brown. The hydrides of this element form cluster types termed closo, nido, and arachno according to Wade's rules. FTP, identify this light element which has the atomic number five.

Folklore from this modern-day country includes a mythical being, called the Squonk, which lives in a hemlock forest and dissolves into its own tears upon being perceived. Other stories from this country feature the trickster Brer Rabbit, who tricks a wolf into throwing him into a briar patch that is actually his home. One figure from this country's folklore legendarily created a huge ravine by dragging his axe and a series of lakes as watering holes for his companion, Babe the Blue Ox. For 10 points, name this country, which is home to tales of the giant Paul Bunyan, who created its Great Lakes and Grand Canyon.

One character in this novel teaches hand signals to Grimaud, and is later trapped in cellar with him, where he consumes all of its food and wine. One character in this novel escapes to Lille to exact revenge on the protagonist by poisoning his love interest. That female character in this novel persuades John Felton to free her and assassinate the Duke of Buckingham. At the end of this novel, the protagonist, who is a hot-blooded Gascon, is promoted when he reveals that he has killed his nemesis Milady de Winter. In this novel, the motto "one for all, and all for one" is proposed by d'Artagnan. For 10 points, name this novel by Alexandre Dumas whose title characters are Athos, Porthos, and Aramis.

This man is shown as a slab of rock propped by a crutch which has a mustache that serves as the wings of the "angel of speech" in a painting titled for him by Salvador Dali; that painting titled for him shows a fully nude Gala slumbering at the right of the dreamworld. In another painting titled for this man, the artist Raphael is led by hand towards this man as he sits on a throne, gestured at by men at the bottom in black Renaissance robes. A scroll and a lyre are offered to this man in that painting, in which a woman in red with a sword and a woman in green with an oar sit at his feet. In another painting, this man is depicted as a statue in a shadowy room, on which another man is resting his hand. Rembrandt depicted "Aristotle with a Bust of" this man, and Ingres depicted his "Apotheosis." For 10 points, name this blind Greek poet of the Iliad.

The capacity of these entities can be written as the derivative of one quantity with respect to the co-logarithm of another quantity. Geologists use the redox variety of these to contain the fugacity of oxygen in minerals, and an ICE table can be used to calculate the equilibrium constant for these entities. One equation related to these entities adds the logarithm of the concentration of a conjugate base over the concentration of an acid and is known as the Henderson-Hasselbach equation. For 10 points, name these systems that use conjugate acids and bases in order to resist pH changes.

In asymptotic giant branch stars, the third dredge-up removes the remnants of a "shell" this element forms around the core. This element is consumed in a reaction that generates power proportional to the square of density and roughly the fortieth power of temperature at around 100 million kelvins. A mechanism for producing this element sometimes produces fluorine as an intermediate and was proposed by Bethe and Weizsäcker. In some low-mass stars, this element's runaway fusion causes its namesake "flash." This element is created via the CNO cycle and the proton-proton chain, and it "burns" in the triple-alpha process. For 10 points, name this element that is created in stars by the fusion of hydrogen.

parts.text: Name this prince of Denmark, the protagonist of a Shakespeare tragedy.
After fighting Hamlet inside a grave, this son of Polonius and brother of Ophelia kills him with a poisoned rapier.

Hamlet's fight with Laertes in a grave is an example of an "objective correlative," a term coined by this author in his critical essay "Hamlet and His Problems," which appears in his collection The Sacred Wood.

bonuses.leadin: This character quips that he is "too much i' the sun" and arranges the deaths of Rosencrantz and Guildenstern. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this location where some people were consumed by Ammit if they failed a test involving an object belonging to Ma'at.

In the test, this body part of dead Egyptians was weighed and compared to the feather of Ma'at. If this body part weighed more than the feather, they were devoured for having insufficient truth and justice.
The god Thoth also hung out in Duat. He was typically depicted as having the head of either a baboon or this other animal.

bonuses.leadin: Those that passed a test were able to pass through this location to Aaru, the Field of Reeds. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Spock's father hails from this planet, which shares its name with the Roman god of fire.
Close relatives of the Vulcans come from this planet, named after a mythical twin of Remus raised by a she-wolf. The people of this planet are known for piloting warbirds.
In the episode "Who Mourns for Adonais?", the Enterprise approaches a planet named for this immortal son of Leda, before being grabbed by a giant green hand.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these planets from Star Trek that share their names with Greco-Roman figures.

parts.text: Robert Filmer's Patriarcha argues that what sort of people have a "divine right" since they are descended from Adam?

The first of these texts is mostly a line-by-line refutation of Filmer's Patriarcha. These texts' claim that legitimate slavery is possible if the enslaved is an unjust aggressor who has been defeated in war has been interpreted by some to include African-American slavery.

Filmer's view that kings are fathers and fathers are kings is dubbed classic patriarchalism in this book. This book argues that the debate between Filmer and Locke did not defeat patriarchalism as traditionally held, but merely transformed it into modern patriarchy.

bonuses.leadin: Foucault's Discipline and Punish analogizes the body of the prisoner to the "two bodies" of this kind of person theorized by Ernst Kantorowicz. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this island in the Gulf of Aden where early explorers believed red sap from "dragon blood" trees was cinnabar. Hadibu is home to the only airport on this island.
The Avenue of the Baobabs lines a road leading to this island country's city of Morondava. This largest island in the Indian Ocean speaks a Malayo-Polynesian language in its capital of Antananarivo.

In the Maldives, blocks from massive coral reefs were used to construct one of these buildings titled Hukuru. In September 2019, renovations to one of these non-Christian buildings in Mayotte was dubbed the sister project to the Notre-Dame renovations.

bonuses.leadin: A test of strength for men on this island was to catch one of the native tahrir ("tah-REER") species of goat with each hand. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this religion founded in 19th Century New England by the author of this religion's namesake Journal, Herald, and Monitor.
The founder of Christian Science was this woman who studied with the healer Phineas Quimby from Maine.
The first edition of this work of Eddy was published in 1875 and is the primary source of Christian Science beliefs.

bonuses.leadin: Practitioners of this faith believe that sickness can be healed by prayer because it is actually an illusion. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This fort, located near Lake Champlain in New York, was captured by the Green Mountain Boys led by Ethan Allen in 1775. A popular brand of pencils also shares this name.
This general surrendered the British Fort Necessity during the French and Indian War. Later, he led the Continental Army against the British during the Revolutionary War.
This fort, built on an artificial island near Charleston, South Carolina, was still unfinished when it was attacked in 1861. That attack on this fort kicked off the American Civil War.

bonuses.leadin: For ten points each, answer some questions about famous forts in American history:

parts.text: In Islamic funerals, the Salat al-Janazah prayer is read and this many handfuls of soil are placed into the ground at 90º to the Qiblah. The Muslim holiday of Eid al-Adha lasts this many days.

In this religion, those above the age of fifteen who die are given a ring during burial that says "I came forth from God." This religion's central book is the Kitab-i-Aqdas, and its founder was a follower of the Bab.

This funerary practice is a common feature of Antyesti rituals for the dead in Hinduism. Widows used to follow their husbands in this practice as part of sati, and many have their ashes poured into the Ganges River after it.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about funerary practices in different religions. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this metal whose cations ("CAT-ai-ons") become intercalated ("in-TUR-kuh-lay-ted") in a graphite matrix in certain devices.
Lithium ions are commonly used in rechargeable types of these devices that store electrical power.
This radioactive isotope used in nuclear fusion is produced by bombarding lithium with neutrons. This isotope is also used for glow-in-the-dark watch dials and gun sights.

bonuses.leadin: This element, aluminum, and hydrogen form a powerful reducing agent used to convert carbonyl ("car-buh-NEEL") groups into alcohols. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with antigen presentation.
What is the main function of the T cell in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to antigen presentation.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with blood pressure regulation.
What is the main function of the systole in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to blood pressure regulation.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this painting depicting several philosophers and mathematicians.
In the center of the painting, Aristotle is seen talking to this other philosopher, his teacher.
The painting is this kind of artwork, a mural painted directly onto wet plaster. This term comes from the Italian word for "fresh."

bonuses.leadin: In this painting by Raphael, Aristotle is seen holding a copy of one of his books, The Nicomachean Ethics. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Austrian founder of psychoanalysis who theorized that the mind is made up of the id, the ego, and the superego.

"Irma's Injection" was one of the title events that Freud analyzed in his book on the Interpretation of these events. Freud argued that these experiences, which happen during sleep, are forms of "wish-fulfilment."
Freud paired this concept with "totem" in the title of a collection of his essays. This term refers to practices that are forbidden by societal rules, such as incest and cannibalism.

bonuses.leadin: This psychologist discussed the "pleasure principle" in his book Civilization and its Discontents. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this usually three day festival which celebrates the end of the month of Ramadan.
Eid al-Adha celebrates Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice this son. This son of Hagar agrees to be sacrificed, unlike his unknowing brother Isaac in the related Judaic story.

On the 12th of Rab' al-awwal, many Muslims celebrate this event which in Indonesia is commemorated by the week long Sekaten festival. Some fundamentalists do not observe it because there is no basis for doing so in the life of the Prophet.

bonuses.leadin: This holiday falls on the first day of Shawwal, and in the last few days of the previous month each family gives donations of food to the needy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this set of theoretical methods based on the Bogolyubov inequality.

An alternative to mean field theory is the approximation named for a guy with this surname and Williams, which assumes the configurational energy is equal to its arithmetic average. A pair with this surname formulated an X-ray diffraction law.

Mean-field theory predicts long-range order and finite critical temperature for the 1-D form of this model, a popular toy model in statistical mechanics. It's a lattice with allowed spins of plus one and minus one at each site.

bonuses.leadin: These methods assumes that local ordering is statistically independent, so the interaction terms in the Hamiltonian of a system are replaced by an "effective" term. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Greek goddess of wisdom. She's the namesake of a city whose symbols are the owl and the olive tree.
In Norse mythology, the skull of one of these creatures named Ymir was used by Odin to create the heavens. These figures resided in Jotunheim.
The skull of Tiamat was smashed by this Babylonian storm god in the Enuma Elish in order to gain the Tablet of Destinies. He was frequently depicted as the head of the Babylonian pantheon.

bonuses.leadin: Zeus thought he would be rid of this daughter of metis after he swallowed her, but she instead sprang fully formed from his head. For 10 points:

parts.text: Name this sort of animal which various people named Cycnus transformed into. Leda was raped by Zeus in the form of one of these birds.
In the Metamorphoses, Achilles kills Neptune's son Cycnus in this manner. Heracles killed the Nemean Lion using this method.
Ovid claims that this person had a friend named Cycnus who lamented him until he turned into a swan as old man. Upon his death, this person's sisters turned into poplar trees which shed amber tears.

bonuses.leadin: Ovid's Metamorphoses discusses a boy who becomes one of these animals after jumping into a lake when Phyllis stops bringing him random animals. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this French neoclassical architect, whose only remaining work in Paris is the Hotel Alexandre.
Boullée is perhaps best known for his proposal for a cenotaph to this man, which consists of a massive sphere surrounded by rows of cypress trees.
This English artist portrayed Newton as a man bending over himself to draw with a compass. This artist is known for a drawing depicting Urizen crouching against a circular background.

bonuses.leadin: This architect frequently considered light in his designs, as exemplified by his Project for a Metropole. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this cyclic organic compound with formula C6H6, whose derivatives include toluene and aniline.
Kekule's model of benzene, with alternating single and double bonds, explains this interaction, where pi electrons are delocalized around a ring, lending stability.
Benzene is the simplest in the family of PAHs. Naphthalene ["nap-tha-leen"], which is found in mothballs, is made of a structure that resembles this number of benzene rings fused together.

bonuses.leadin: Dewar's model of this compound was made nearly 100 years after its proposal, and an isomer of this compound, bicyclopropenyl ["by-cy-clo-pro-pen-ill"], was synthesized in 1989. For 10 points each:

parts.text: AIBN is an example of what kind of substance that undergoes a homolytic bond cleavage in order to start a radical reaction?
The decomposition of AIBN is driven by the release of this molecule. In the Haber process, this diatomic gas reacts with hydrogen to form ammonia, and this gas is the most common in the atmosphere.

Another popular initiator contains this metal bonded to three butyl groups and a hydride. This metal is bonded to several butyl and isothiocyanate groups in Otera's catalyst, which is used for transesterification.

bonuses.leadin: Popular examples of these substances include organic peroxides such as di-tert-butyl peroxide, which easily decompose to form two oxygen radicals. For 10 points each:
